reason: The text contains multiple named character figures with dialogue, emotional expressions, and individual perspectives. The people of Israel speak collectively ('We are your bone and flesh'), expressing their allegiance. The Jebusites speak with defiance. David expresses longing/desire ('Who will give me water from the well of Bethlehem'), moral conviction (refusing to drink the water and explaining his reasoning through an appeal to the men's lives), and strategic opinion (declaring that whoever strikes the Jebusites first will be chief). The text portrays various mighty men (Joab, Eleazar, Abishai, Benaiah, and others) with individual deeds and accomplishments, suggesting personality and agency. While these are not entirely 'ordinary' people (many are leaders and warriors), they are presented as human characters with individual lines, emotional motivations, and expressed viewpoints rather than merely as agents of divine will.
